messages:
Emily: heads up — canary 2026.03.17-prod-kernels showed a p99 tail jump after the kernel-selector change, rolling back now. logs below.

Emily: ```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] model=redwood-xl kernel_selector=v2 p95=78ms p99=420ms gpu_util=72% kernel_dispatch=3.9ms
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] model=redwood-xl kernel_selector=v2 p95=82ms p99=1120ms gpu_util=84% kernel_dispatch=12.4ms kv_miss=0.42
```

Raj: ugh. any config diffs? microbatching or kv-warmup toggled? :eyes:

Sasha: quick summary from profiler: kernel_selector:v2 added an extra fallback probe that runs per-request when kvcache warmness < 0.6. probe does a small matmul to test fast-kernel compatibility — adds ~8-12ms on path when it picks scalar fallback.

Diego: repro'd locally with a synthetic trace. microbatch went 8 -> 16 due to batching heuristic change, which increased concurrency and made kv warm rate drop (bigger batches serialized more seqs with cold kv). saw kvmiss spike at startup.

Raj: so two effects: 1) larger microbatches reduce per-request warmups, 2) selector probe triggers heavy fallback at high util. combined -> p99s.

Emily: can we gate the selector probe on headroom? i.e., only run the expensive compatibility check if GPU util < X and kv_warmness < Y?

Sasha: proposed rule: "if predicted_gpu_util > 0.78 then avoid probe and prefer previously-successful kernel variant; if kv_warmness < 0.4, schedule background kv-prefetch and mark request as provisional for fast-kernel decisions."

Raj: sketch of admission pseudocode: ```
if gpu_util_estimate >= 0.78:
  kernel_choice = sticky_last_working_variant(request.model, request.shape)
else:
  if kv_warmness < 0.5:
    trigger_background_kv_prefetch(request.prefix)
  kernel_choice = run_selector_probe(request)
```

Diego: background prefetch idea is good. but prefetch itself can thrash memory if we overrun bandwidth. we should rate-limit prefetches per-GPU: ``prefetch_budget=5/s`` and cancel if util > 0.8.

Sasha: agreed. also maybe switch probe from sync to async: do probe in parallel with first token emission. if probe fails later, route fallback tokens via shorter kernel path or slow-path without blocking p95. that reduces tail amplification.

Emily: that matches our goals: keep p95 stable, accept small p99 regressions only if necessary, but avoid >2x p99 spikes. Ops wants headroom preserved.

Raj: short-term mitigation: revert kernel_selector change (already rolling back). medium-term: implement headroom-aware gating + async probe + prefetch budget. long-term: adjust batching heuristic to cap microbatch at 12 for bursty traffic shapes.

Diego: I'll run a simulation with the cap=12 and prefetch_budget=5/s and generate a headroom vs throughput curve. expecting p99 improvement ~30% on our canary traces.

perf-bot: summary report: https://internal.perf/reports/2026-03-17/canary-kerndump (contains heap profiles, kernel dispatch traces, kv miss heatmap). :link:

Emily: ack. Diego/ Sasha — can we have a PR with the gating + async probe prototype by tomorrow EOD? we can dogfood on staging then promote.

Sasha: yep, will open draft PR with tests and perf microbench results.

Raj: also add a smoke test that forces kv_miss=1.0 and verifies probe doesn't block p95.

Emily: thanks. I'll keep the rollback active until the staging run looks good. :thumbsup:

Diego: adding note to runbook: if p99 > 2x baseline, toggle kernel-selector -> v1 and reduce microbatch cap to 8 until canary stabilizes.

Emily: perfect. catching this early saved us.

perf-bot: reaction :point_up: (automated anomaly spike flagged at 14:02:12 UTC)
